 This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant challenging the dismissal of the claim petition in MVC No.66/2021 dated 13.10.2022 passed by the learned Prl. District and Sessions Judge & MACT Raichur (for short 'the Tribunal').
2.

entities.text: Prl. District and Sessions Judge & MACT Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Though this appeal is listed for admission, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the impugned judgment and award passed by the tribunal is contrary to the material evidence placed before the tribunal.

The tribunal is not justified in dismissing the claim petition on the ground that in Ex.P2 -inquest panchanama the only name of the mother is shown as Smt.Kokonda Renuka W/o; Late Sathyanarayana, but in the claim petition of the cause title shows that Ashwini @ Renuka.
However, she has failed to peace of papers that both names are one and the same.

At the time of assigning the reasons the learned tribunal has totally ignored Ex.P6-death certificate wherein it reveals shows the address and name of the mother is Kokonda Renuka @ Ashwini in the column of address mentioned at H.No.56, Chandra Bandoa Road, Ashraya Colony, Riachur.

Hence, on these grounds sought for allowing of the appeal and seeks to set aside the impugned judgment and award passed by the tribunal and prays to remand the matter to the tribunal for fresh consideration in accordance with law.

5. A perusal of paragraph Nos.10 to 12 of the impugned judgment wherein the tribunal has observed as follows;
10. Issue No.2: Issue No.2 is with regard to the petitioner for compensation.
The petitioner has claimed total compensation Rs.33,50,000/- claiming herself to be the genetic mother of the deceased Kokonda Kaushik and dependent upon him.
It is therefore, heavy burden cast upon the petitioner to prove that she is the mother of the deceased boy and was dependent upon his income.
Let us examine whether the petitioner is able to prove her relationship with deceased boy.
After careful examination of the materials on record, I am of the opinion that the petitioner miserably failed to prove her relationship with the deceased boy.

It is so because, according to the details of the relatives mentioned in the inquest panchanama marked at Ex.P.2. which is in Telugu language, its translation is marked at Ex.P.2(a), in all four persons are shown to be the relatives of the deceased boy.

Among them, relative No.2's name has been shown as Smt. Kokonda Renuka W/o Late Sathyanarayana, R/0:

2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Bapu Nagar, Chikadapalli, Chikadapalli, Secundrabad, as mother of deceased.

But according to the petitioner herself after the death of her first husband Mr.
Sathyanarayana, she married Eashwar Singh Takur, therefore, heavy burden cast upon the petitioner to prove that she is the same lady as mentioned in Sl. no.2 of Ex P.2(a) as Smt. Kokonda Renuka.

But on perusal of the cause title of the petition her name has been shown as Ashwini @ Renuka, but she failed to produce any plece of reliable paper to show that she is the same lady, who was called as Renuka, who married deceased Sathyanarayana and after her second marriage with Eashwar Singh Takur she got changed her name as Ashwini @ Renuka.
unfortunate thing is that not a single piece of reliable documentary evidence is produced nor she able to examine any of the relatives of her so called first deceased husband.
11. Unless the petitioner proves her relationship with the deceased, she is not entitled to claim any compensation.
This is about the proof of relationship.

Assume for the sake of argument, the petitioner is the mother of the deceased, even then question arises whether she was depending upon the deceased, because admittedly accident took place within the territorial jurisdiction of Ghatkeshwar P.S. of Rachakonda District in Telangan State.
According to the contents of the complaint and panchanama he was residing with the other relatives in Telangan State Itself.
However, the contention of the petitioner is that the deceased boy was residing with her.
It is therefore, it is the who has to prove that at the time of accident the deceased boy was residing with her, unfortunately the petitioner has not produced any iota of evidence in this regard.
12. Under the circumstances, it is hardly possible to accept that the petitioner is the mother of the deceased boy and she was depending upon him and his income as on the date of the accident.

When the petitioner failed to prove all these things as contended by the respondent counsel the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation, therefore, the issue No.2 under discussion is answered in the negative.

6. A perusal of the claim petition discloses the name of petitioner as Ashwini @ Renuka W/o:
Eashwar Singh Takur and in the column NO.1 of the claim petition name of the deceased is shown as Kokonda Kaushik S/o: Satyanarayana.
In column No.20 the relation with deceased is shown as mother.
The respondent No.1 has not filed any objection.
Respondent No.2 filed written statement but has not specifically denied the relationship between the deceased son Kokonda Kaushik and petitioner Ashwini @ Renuka.
Further, the tribunal has not framed any issue with regard to relationship between the deceased and petitioner.
To substantiate the case of the petitioner, she herself examined as PW.1.
In her evidence, she has clearly stated with regard to relationship between the petitioner and deceased son Kokonda Kaushik.
Ex.P2-inquest panchanama reveals the name of the mother as Kokonda Renuka w/o; Late Satyanarayana.
In the charge sheet-P5, the mother of deceased is shown as Smt.Kokkonda Renuka W/O; Late Satyanarayana.

In Ex.P6-death certificate issued by the Department of Municipal Administration, Medchal-Malkajgiri District of Telangana Government in which the name of deceased is mentioned as Kokona Kaushik and name of mother is mentioned as Kokona Renuka @ Ashwini.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Ex.P7 is the Original Hall ticket issued by Telangana State Board wherein the name of deceased is shown as Kokonda Kaushik, father name is shown as Kokonda Satyanarayan and Mother name is shown as Kokonda Renuka.

sentences.text: of cross examination of PW.1, the resopndent No.2 has not disputed the documentary evidence placed by the petitioner so also the relationship between the petitioner and deceased Kokonda Kaushik.

Hence, the petitioner has placed sufficient oral and documentary evidence to prove that petitioner is mother of deceased Kokonda Kaushik, but the tribunal has not properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence in a proper manner and dismiss the claim petition which is not sustainable in law.
Hence, the matter is remanded to the tribunal to award just and reasonable compensation.
Therefore, it is held that the petitioner is mother of deceased Kokonda Kaushik.

7. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDER  (a) The appeal is allowed and remanded.
(b) The judgment and award passed by the tribunal is  set aside.
(c) The matter is remitted back to the tribunal to Award compensation in accordance with law by providing opportunity to both parties to adduce their further evidence, if any.
(d) Both parties shall appear before the tribunal, on 30.05.2023 without awaiting any further notice.
Thereafter, the tribunal shall dispose of the case within an outer limit of six months from the date of appearance of both the parties.
(e) Registry is directed to send the copy of the judgment along with TCR to the concerned Court.
